audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht studies health, disease and healthcare across Europe. The programme combines epidemiology and research methods with health systems, public policy, ethics and a supervised research placement.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines disease and epidemiology with research methods, EU law and politics. The second explores the social and behavioural factors that affect health and how public messages reach people. Maastricht has dedicated courses in European health systems and a required placement and thesis.

notes.text: The Bachelor European Public Health combines public health epidemiology, health policy and law in the European Union, health systems and health technology with a programme-wide methods line and a placement with thesis. At UCR, students can approach public health through fields such as epidemiology, biomedicine, health psychology, sociology, EU law and politics and sustainability. These programmes therefore offer related perspectives rather than reproducing a full public health curriculum.

The Bachelor European Public Health includes a more extensive sequence in European health policy, health systems and health law, environmental health and health technology. At UCR, students can study epidemiology, disease, EU law and politics and sustainability, but UCR does not offer the same depth or sequence in public health.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

BENECON314.text: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
